title: Proverbs: skill for ordinary days

lines: Wisdom in Proverbs isn't cleverness or book learning. It's skill in living: the ability to see how God's world works and to act in step with it.
Its motto comes in the first chapter.
The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge.

scripture.text: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge

lines: Proverbs is a collection of collections. Nine chapters of longer poems. The proverbs of Solomon. The words of the wise. A second collection copied by Hezekiah's men. And the words of Agur and Lemuel.
The book pictures life as a road with two paths. Choices that look small, a companion, a loan, a glance, a lie, set a person on one road or the other.
Proverbs trains you to see where a path ends before you step onto it.

scripture.text: The path of the righteous is like the first gleam of dawn

lines: In chapters one, eight, and nine, wisdom speaks as a woman who calls out in public places, and who was there with God when he made the world. Her rival, Folly, calls too.
So choosing wisdom means accepting an invitation, not only mastering a set of rules.

scripture.text: Wisdom calls out in the street, she lifts her voice in the square

lines: Few subjects get more attention in Proverbs than the tongue. Honest lips and lying lips. Gossip and discretion. Flattery and faithful rebuke.
A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
Restraint in speech is treated again and again as a mark of wisdom.

scripture.text: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.

chapters.kicker: Watch for: work, money and the poor
lines: Proverbs praises diligence and warns the sluggard. But it also warns against trusting riches and against oppressing the poor.
Wealth is a real good in this book, but always a lesser one than wisdom, righteousness, and a good name.

scripture.text: Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD

lines: Read Proverbs as proverbs. A proverb is a compressed observation about how life usually goes under God. It isn't a guarantee for every case.
Start with chapter one. The key chapters are one, three, eight, nine, ten, twenty-two, and thirty-one.
It's skill for ordinary days, and it begins here.
Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and lean not on your own understanding.

scripture.text: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and lean not on your own understanding
